failure_mode: surfacing internal implementation details as user-facing action items
description: Jarvis repeatedly surfaced Plaud token as a blocker requiring manual user action, asking David to run the Chrome login flow. David corrected: token handling is fully autonomous within the Knox/plaud-ingest script. Jarvis should not expose this as a user-facing item.
what_went_wrong: Treated Knox's internal workflow concern (API auth) as something David needed to manually resolve. This is cognitive load on the controller for issues the system handles on its own.
fix: Never surface Plaud token requirements in briefings. If plaud-ingest hits a token blocker, Knox handles it. Only bubble up to David if Knox truly fails to retry, which is rare. Trust the automation.
how_to_prevent: Review boot briefing guidelines: only surface blockers that require David's direct action. Internal workflow concerns (authentication, retries, queueing) stay internal unless they genuinely break the flow.
